attempts.summary:
Configured redundant L3 connectivity between node1's private network (node3) and node2's private network (node4) carried over both independent node1-node2 links, with automatic failover and full node-restart persistence verified on all four nodes.

Topology discovery: node1 eth1/eth2 and node2 eth1/eth2 are the two independent uplinks between node1-node2; node1 eth3 connects to node3's enp8s0, node2 eth3 connects to node4's enp8s0 (confirmed via targeted ping tests, since interfaces carried no IPs initially).

Implementation:
- node1: bond0 (Linux bonding, mode balance-rr, miimon 100) over eth1+eth2, IP 172.20.0.1/30 to node2; eth3 = 192.168.1.1/24 (node3's subnet). IP forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. Static route to 192.168.2.0/24 via bond0.
- node2: mirrored — bond0 172.20.0.2/30, eth3 = 192.168.2.1/24 (node4's subnet), route to 192.168.1.0/24 via bond0.
- node3/node4: enp8s0 statically addressed (192.168.1.2/24, 192.168.2.2/24) via existing NetworkManager profiles with a static route to the other private subnet via its local node1/node2 gateway — persists natively through NetworkManager.
- Persistence on node1/node2: a systemd oneshot unit (antrieb-links.service, enabled, WantedBy=multi-user.target) reapplies the bonding/IP/forwarding/route configuration at boot, since SONiC's interfaces-config.service only manages eth0/lo and does not touch eth1-3.
- Discovered and worked around a virtio/bonding limitation: 802.3ad (LACP) mode failed because virtio-net can't report link speed/duplex (dmesg: "failed to get link speed/duplex"), so switched to balance-rr, which works cleanly and actively load-balances across both links (confirmed via matched tx_packet counters growing symmetrically on eth1/eth2 for a test ping burst).
- Also discovered that the platform's virtual point-to-point links do not propagate one-sided admin-down to the peer's carrier state (verified: bringing node1's eth1 down did not clear LOWER_UP on node2's eth1), so failover was correctly demonstrated as a full link outage (both endpoints down), which is the realistic failure model — 0% packet loss for node3↔node4 traffic in that state, and clean automatic recovery once both ends were restored.
- Ran the mandatory node-restart protocol on all four nodes sequentially (one at a time, quorum/service preserved): captured pre-restart boot_id, restarted via `reboot`/`systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed a new boot_id, and verified bonding/routes/forwarding/NetworkManager config and node3↔node4 connectivity recovered on each.
